Unsupported or misleading claims to remove

1. Universal eligibility
   - “Every company under 50 is eligible.”
   - “If you have fewer than 50 seats, you qualify.”
   - “Any small team can use Helio Start.”
   Why unsupported: seat count is only one factor. Eligibility also depends on entitlement, admin authority, supported billing, connector access, external-system authority, and setup fit.

2. Immediate admission or setup
   - “Start now.”
   - “You’re ready to set up.”
   - “Get approved and begin immediately.”
   - “Start with Helio Start.”
   Why unsupported: an eligibility check does not confirm admission, and the self-serve path still requires review of the applicable gates.

3. Universal support for excluded or assisted scenarios
   - “Imports and migrations are included in Helio Start.”
   - “We support every billing arrangement.”
   - “Any permissions or deployment model will work.”
   Why unsupported: imports, migrations, complex deployments, manual billing, agency access, unsupported permissions, and unresolved ownership may require assisted handling or may remain outside the path.

4. Elimination or trivialization of assisted routing
   - “Everyone can complete setup themselves.”
   - “Assisted setup is only an optional upgrade.”
   - “If you do not qualify for Start, there is no next step.”
   Why unsupported: assisted routing remains an intentional route for cases requiring review or help. It does not guarantee admission or convert unsupported requirements into eligibility.

Heading:
Helio Start for straightforward teams under 50

Body:
Check whether your team fits the standard Helio Start path. Eligibility depends on factors such as current entitlement, supported billing, verified admin access, connector authentication, external-system authority, and setup fit. Checking eligibility does not confirm admission or immediate setup.

CTA:
Check eligibility

Block 2 — assisted path

Heading:
Need a different setup path?

Body:
If your team needs help with ownership, permissions, connector access, migration, imports, complex deployment, manual billing, or another setup requirement, request a review. We’ll assess the request and route it to the appropriate path before any admission decision.

CTA:
Request assisted review

Shorter version

Check eligibility for the standard Helio Start path. Requirements include supported billing, verified admin and system access, connector and external-system authority, and a setup that fits the path. Historical baseline — not a live policy change

Scope
Baseline the approved public-path admission checklist as it stood on 2024-04-23, then append the later connector-access input. Admission requires every input below; a missing or unresolved input keeps the case out of the admitted path. “No” or “Not sure” for connector access is pending/assisted before admission, not an admission.

I2  Helio admin proof: verified current admin access/ownership
I3  Deployment: simple/standard deployment
I4  First-week integration fit: a supported first integration can be connected within week one
I5  Entitlement: current entitlement state
I6  Billing: supported billing; no manual-billing exception
I7  Connector access: definite confirmation that the selected connector can be authenticated during setup in week one (later input; stored separately from Helio admin proof)

Regression cases

A0 — admitted baseline
All inputs present: I1 yes; I2 yes; I3 yes; I4 yes; I5 current; I6 supported; I7 definite Yes. Result: admitted through the ordinary public-path gate.

N1 — non-admitted: I1 missing

N2 — non-admitted: I2 missing
I2 absent; I1 and I3–I7 present. Result: not admitted; Helio admin proof is unresolved. No other input is missing.

N3 — non-admitted: I3 missing

N4 — non-admitted: I4 missing

sources.label: Assistant's reply to Riley Tanaka, message 001787
excerpts:
Marcus — I would not approve the $100,000 Q3 paid-acquisition test or attach a pipeline claim to this result.

The completed Helio Start cohort supports a bounded organic conclusion:

- 52 of 52 workspaces have mature day-90 windows.
- 39 were paid and active at the day-90 snapshot.
- 7 had canceled before day 90.
- 4 were past due.
- 2 were on billing hold.

The four statuses reconcile to the full cohort. The 39/52 result is therefore useful descriptive evidence that Helio Start can operate as an organic pricing-page product motion. It is not, by itself, a retention-rate, acquisition, causal, or pipeline result.

The acquisition and pipeline leap is not decision-safe for three reasons:

1. No acquisition-cost comparison exists. This is an organic cohort, so we do not know what paid spend would be required to produce comparable workspaces, what the incremental conversion would be, or whether the motion could support acceptable CAC, payback, contribution margin, or LTV/CAC.

2. First-paid, activation, and paid-active answer different questions from unit economics. First-paid establishes that a qualifying payment occurred; activation establishes product behavior; paid-active establishes billing/entitlement status at a specified snapshot. None establishes revenue durability, gross margin, support or servicing cost, acquisition cost, payback period, or forecastable lifetime value.

3. The denominator cannot be narrowed to the favorable status. Omitting the 7 canceled, 4 past-due, and 2 billing-hold workspaces would turn a complete 52-workspace status table into an unsupported success claim and would obscure material outcome states.

Decision: keep Helio Start available as a bounded organic pricing-page channel through Q3, with the existing refusal rules and connector-access check. Do not authorize the $100,000 paid-acquisition test or create a Q3 pipeline claim from this cohort. Reconsider only after we have a defined paid test or credible acquisition-cost benchmark, incremental attribution, revenue and margin data, and mature retention/payback evidence.

First-paid establishes that a qualifying payment occurred; activation establishes product behavior; paid-active establishes billing/entitlement status at a specified snapshot. None establishes revenue durability, gross margin, support or servicing cost, acquisition cost, payback period, or forecastable lifetime value.

3. The denominator cannot be narrowed to the favorable status. Omitting the 7 canceled, 4 past-due, and 2 billing-hold workspaces would turn a complete 52-workspace status table into an unsupported success claim and would obscure material outcome states.

Decision: keep Helio Start available as a bounded organic pricing-page channel through Q3, with the existing refusal rules and connector-access check. Marcus’s calculation is arithmetically correct:

$18,960 ÷ 52 workspaces = $364.615..., or $364.62 per workspace rounded.

But the label “allowable paid-acquisition CAC” is not correct.

What the figure actually represents is:

“Average refund-adjusted cash observed per admitted workspace in the mature Helio Start organic cohort.”

It is a realized-cash observation from 52 workspaces that arrived through the organic motion. It does not tell us what Helio would have to spend to acquire a workspace through paid media.

Paid CAC requires, at minimum:

- identifiable paid-media and related acquisition costs;
- a clearly defined paid-acquired workspace denominator;
- channel attribution;
- evidence that the workspaces were incremental rather than merely reclassified organic demand; and
- a paid-channel response or comparison showing the resulting conversion and quality.

None of that is present here. The $364.62 numerator is cash collected from workspaces, not acquisition spend. Dividing it by the cohort size therefore produces an average organic cash-per-workspace figure, not a cost of acquiring a workspace.

The mature evidence remains useful. The 52-workspace cohort has complete retention-status information, refund-adjusted cash matched at the account level, and classified support effort. Together, those measures can inform a later paid-acquisition proposal by showing realized cash, outcome durability, and servicing burden. They still cannot be relabeled as paid CAC or used alone to authorize a paid test.

Decision-safe wording:

“Helio Start generated $18,960 in refund-adjusted cash across 52 mature organic workspaces, or $364.62 average cash per admitted workspace. This is an observed organic-cohort cash metric, not paid CAC. The cohort contains no paid-media cost, acquisition-mix, or incremental paid-channel comparison, so it does not establish the cost of acquiring a workspace through paid acquisition or authorize a paid test.”

Marcus — I would not approve the $100,000 Q3 paid-acquisition test or attach a pipeline claim to this result.

input.title: Helio Start 2028 paid-acquisition proposal readiness checklist
input.body:
Helio Start 2028 paid-acquisition proposal readiness checklist

Effective date: January 1, 2028

Purpose

Use this checklist for every 2028 Helio Start paid-acquisition proposal. It is a readiness gate, not budget approval, paid-traffic authorization, launch approval, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, or a causal acquisition claim.

Gate: no budget or channel tactics before mature evidence is complete

Do not discuss or settle a budget, audience, channel, spend level, traffic cap, bid strategy, or other channel tactic until the evidence package below is complete, internally reconciled, and explicitly certified. A first-paid count, activation result, paid-active snapshot, signup-start target, or proposed spend is not sufficient.

Required mature evidence

[ ] Two consecutive mature cohorts are identified with fixed denominators, exact cohort dates, and complete day-90 outcome windows.

[ ] Each cohort includes the full mutually exclusive day-90 status table: paid-active, canceled, past due, and billing hold. Keep every outcome in the denominator; do not report only the favorable status.

[ ] Mature retention/outcome evidence is paired with refund-adjusted collected cash, matched at account level to the same cohort and reconciliation period. Gross billed cash may be shown, but it must remain distinct from refund-adjusted collected cash.

[ ] Account-level support effort is complete from first contact, includes zero-contact accounts in the denominator, preserves assisted-route context, and distinguishes product support from unrelated pre-admission connector-authority or billing contacts. Report the distribution and high-support tail, not only an average.

[ ] For the reopening condition, both consecutive mature cohorts have fewer than 5% of accounts exceeding 90 account-level support minutes, and no unsupported case entered the admitted path. Any exception or unresolved classification blocks readiness.

[ ] A paid-channel bridge exists: either a defined paid test or a credible acquisition-cost benchmark, with identifiable paid cost, a defined paid-acquired denominator, credible final-route attribution, and evidence addressing incrementality rather than reclassifying organic demand.

[ ] The package contains mature paid-cohort retention/payback and revenue/margin treatment where a paid result is being proposed. Organic-cohort cash and support results must not be relabeled as paid CAC, paid-channel unit economics, or paid performance.

[ ] Source completeness, account joins, denominators, status meanings, refund treatment, attribution, and support classifications are reconciled. Any missing, disputed, or immature lane is visibly marked and prevents the gate from clearing.

How the evidence must be combined

Combine the evidence in one decision package, but do not collapse it into one blended score or substitute one measure for another. The package must show, side by side and with shared account/cohort identity where applicable:

1. Mature day-90 retention/outcome status, including all mutually exclusive outcome states and the complete denominator.
2. Refund-adjusted collected cash, with gross billed cash and refunds separately visible.
3. Account-level support effort, including zero-contact accounts, first-contact continuity, assisted routing, and the high-support tail.
4. Paid acquisition cost or credible benchmark, final-route attribution, and incremental-outcome evidence.
5. Mature paid-cohort quality, revenue/margin treatment, and payback when the proposal relies on paid results.

The combined package may support discussion of whether a bounded paid proposal is decision-ready. It does not turn organic observations into paid CAC, and it does not create a pipeline target, forecast credit, scalable acquisition claim, or launch authorization. First-paid, activation, and paid-active status may be included as descriptive or leading measures, but never as substitutes for mature retention, cash, support, acquisition-cost, attribution, or incrementality evidence.

Package responsibility

Owen and Customer Success jointly own producing and certifying the combined evidence package. Do not invent separate owners for retention, cash, support effort, or any other evidence category; those measures remain jointly owned and must remain separate at account level.

Riley Tanaka may assemble and prepare the proposal package after the evidence gate and proposal-preparation authority are explicitly cleared. That preparation role does not transfer evidence ownership or approve budget, traffic, channel tactics, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, or launch. Priya’s decision and any separate budget and implementation approvals remain required.

Final readiness check

[ ] Every required evidence line is complete, mature, reconciled, and certified by the joint package owners.
[ ] The combined read is decision-safe and keeps each measure separate at account level.
[ ] No organic metric is labeled as paid acquisition economics.
[ ] The proposal clearly distinguishes preparation from approval and launch.
[ ] Remaining approval gates are named without presenting placeholders as settled decisions.

If any box is unchecked: stop at evidence completion. Do not discuss or settle budget or channel tactics.

[ ] Each cohort includes the full mutually exclusive day-90 status table: paid-active, canceled, past due, and billing hold. Keep every outcome in the denominator; do not report only the favorable status.

[ ] Mature retention/outcome evidence is paired with refund-adjusted collected cash, matched at account level to the same cohort and reconciliation period. Gross billed cash may be shown, but it must remain distinct from refund-adjusted collected cash.

[ ] Account-level support effort is complete from first contact, includes zero-contact accounts in the denominator, preserves assisted-route context, and distinguishes product support from unrelated pre-admission connector-authority or billing contacts. Report the distribution and high-support tail, not only an average.

[ ] For the reopening condition, both consecutive mature cohorts have fewer than 5% of accounts exceeding 90 account-level support minutes, and no unsupported case entered the admitted path. Any exception or unresolved classification blocks readiness.

[ ] A paid-channel bridge exists: either a defined paid test or a credible acquisition-cost benchmark, with identifiable paid cost, a defined paid-acquired denominator, credible final-route attribution, and evidence addressing incrementality rather than reclassifying organic demand.

[ ] The package contains mature paid-cohort retention/payback and revenue/margin treatment where a paid result is being proposed. Organic-cohort cash and support results must not be relabeled as paid CAC, paid-channel unit economics, or paid performance.

[ ] Source completeness, account joins, denominators, status meanings, refund treatment, attribution, and support classifications are reconciled. Any missing, disputed, or immature lane is visibly marked and prevents the gate from clearing.

How the evidence must be combined

Combine the evidence in one decision package, but do not collapse it into one blended score or substitute one measure for another. The package must show, side by side and with shared account/cohort identity where applicable:

1. Mature day-90 retention/outcome status, including all mutually exclusive outcome states and the complete denominator.
2. Refund-adjusted collected cash, with gross billed cash and refunds separately visible.
3. Account-level support effort, including zero-contact accounts, first-contact continuity, assisted routing, and the high-support tail.
4. Paid acquisition cost or credible benchmark, final-route attribution, and incremental-outcome evidence.
5. Mature paid-cohort quality, revenue/margin treatment, and payback when the proposal relies on paid results.

It does not turn organic observations into paid CAC, and it does not create a pipeline target, forecast credit, scalable acquisition claim, or launch authorization. First-paid, activation, and paid-active status may be included as descriptive or leading measures, but never as substitutes for mature retention, cash, support, acquisition-cost, attribution, or incrementality evidence.

Riley Tanaka may assemble and prepare the proposal package after the evidence gate and proposal-preparation authority are explicitly cleared. That preparation role does not transfer evidence ownership or approve budget, traffic, channel tactics, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, or launch. Priya’s decision and any separate budget and implementation approvals remain required.

Final readiness check

[ ] Every required evidence line is complete, mature, reconciled, and certified by the joint package owners.
[ ] The combined read is decision-safe and keeps each measure separate at account level.
[ ] No organic metric is labeled as paid acquisition economics.
[ ] The proposal clearly distinguishes preparation from approval and launch.
[ ] Remaining approval gates are named without presenting placeholders as settled decisions.

If any box is unchecked: stop at evidence completion. Do not discuss or settle budget or channel tactics.

input.title: CS auto-nudge historical evidence scorecard — 2028-01-01
input.body:
CS auto-nudge historical evidence scorecard
As of: 2028-01-01
Replay scope: 412 recent CS auto-nudge decisions replayed against the shared-state contract.

1. Scorecard

Grand total: 412

- Legacy-result matches: 386
  - Category total: 386

- Non-matches: 26
  - Category total: 26
  - Field-specific holds: 19
    - Category subtotal: 19
    - Stale qualifying-human-admin state: 15
    - Unresolved external-system authority: 4
  - Suppressions: 7
    - Category subtotal: 7
    - Active Customer Success adoption or renewal work: 7

No non-match was unmatched or unclassified.

2. Reconciliation checks

- Field-specific holds: 15 + 4 = 19. Verified.
- Non-matches: 19 holds + 7 suppressions = 26. Verified.
- Grand total: 386 matches + 26 non-matches = 412. Verified.
- Independent full-category check: 386 + 15 + 4 + 7 = 412. Verified.

All cause subtotals equal their parent category, and all top-level categories equal the replay denominator.

3. What the non-matches mean under the shared-state contract

The 26 non-matches are not unexplained data discrepancies. They are the operating consequences of applying the contract instead of allowing the legacy eligibility result to proceed:

- The 19 field-specific holds are fail-closed outcomes. The required state was not acceptable for release because qualifying-human-admin state was stale in 15 records, or external-system authority remained unresolved in four. The hold preserves field-level visibility and prevents reuse of an unsupported legacy eligibility result.

- The seven suppressions are contract-directed suppressions because current Customer Success adoption or renewal work was active. They are distinct from field-specific holds: the state represents an active competing Customer Success motion, so the nudge is suppressed rather than released.

The contract requires separately governed fields, explicit source ownership and freshness, and fail-closed treatment for stale, unresolved, or conflicting required state. Its semantics do not turn a current transport timestamp into proof that a field is current, and external-system authority means verified readiness for the required connector permission or network action—not blanket permission for automated contact.

4. Current and supported state

No record with all required state current and supported changed outcome in the replay. The seven active-Customer-Success records remain contract-driven suppressions, not unexplained changes or evidence of a clean, proceed-eligible record changing outcome. The 19 holds reflect exactly the cases where the contract found stale or unresolved required state and therefore prevented proceeding.

Conclusion: 386 decisions agreed with the legacy result; the remaining 26 were fully accounted for by governed holds or suppressions. The replay provides evidence of contract control and reconciliation, not a claim about revenue, conversion, or broader customer impact.

- Scope: the single Q2 2027 Helio Start high-intent paid-search test considered at Priya’s Friday, April 9, 2027 budget-and-launch decision.

- Result: 8/8 reached the expected admission route.
- Attribution: paid source reconciled for every case from eligibility-flow start through the expected final route.
- Completed by: Daniela Schultz, who completed the fresh 24-case nonproduction preflight and the end-to-end paid-source reconciliation.
- Verified by: Ines Kovac verified that no case bypassed an existing lifecycle branch, hold, or suppression. Customer Success’s verification also covered the ability to record assisted-route reasons and support minutes from first contact where applicable; it did not change admission meaning.

2. Expected assisted route — 8 cases
- Result: 8/8 reached the expected assisted route.
- Attribution: paid source reconciled for every case from eligibility-flow start through the expected final route.
- Completed by: Daniela Schultz, as the preflight executor and attribution reconciler.
- Verified by: Ines Kovac verified that the route did not bypass an existing lifecycle branch, hold, or suppression. Customer Success verified that the assisted-route reason and account-level support minutes can be recorded from first contact.

3. Expected fail-closed or suppressed route — 8 cases
- Result: 8/8 reached the expected fail-closed or suppressed outcome.
- Attribution: paid source reconciled for every case from eligibility-flow start through the expected final route.
- Completed by: Daniela Schultz, as the preflight executor and attribution reconciler.
- Verified by: Ines Kovac verified that existing lifecycle branches, holds, and suppressions were respected. No case was admitted or assisted through a paid-source bypass. Customer Success’s support-recording verification remained separate from, and did not override, fail-closed or suppression behavior.

Cross-case controls
- Daniela Schultz completed the required fresh 24-case nonproduction preflight.
- Ines Kovac verified that no case bypassed any existing lifecycle branch, hold, or suppression.
- Customer Success verified that assisted-route reasons and support minutes can be captured from first contact.

- No state meaning, eligibility condition, refusal rule, lifecycle behavior, instrumentation meaning, assisted-routing behavior, fail-closed behavior, or owner authority changed.

Historical conclusion
- The evidence card records a cleared technical preflight only. Priya retained the separate authority to decide whether to approve the $8,000 maximum budget and April 12 launch, subject to the unchanged operating boundaries above.

input.title: Incomplete-setup reminder — initial production interval evidence card
input.body:
Historical evidence card

Subject: Incomplete-setup reminder — initial limited-production interval before expansion
Evidence window: October 6–18, 2027
Release during interval: unchanged 10% of otherwise eligible production evaluations
Closed by: Owen
Recorded for the annual controls package: January 1, 2028

Scope and evaluation rule
Every possible display was freshly evaluated against current entitlement, qualifying-human-admin status, incomplete-setup status, and active Customer Success work. Prior shadow-eligible outcomes were not reused. Active Customer Success adoption or renewal work suppressed the reminder; missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting required state was held fail-closed; and the approved customer action remained in-product only.

Disposition reconciliation
Total fresh evaluations: 3,240

- Displayed: 412. The current conditions for the in-product incomplete-setup reminder were met, including qualifying human admin, current active entitlement, incomplete setup, and no active Customer Success adoption or renewal work.
- Suppressed: 138. Current Customer Success work was active, so the reminder was suppressed.
- Held: 61. Required state was missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting, so the evaluation was held fail-closed rather than displayed.
- No display: 2,629. The current incomplete-setup or qualifying-human-admin condition was not met, so no reminder was displayed.

Reconciliation check: 412 + 138 + 61 + 2,629 = 3,240 fresh evaluations. The four dispositions are mutually accounted for and cover the full interval denominator.

Control outcomes
- Cross-surface agreement: Reporting, lifecycle, and reminder outcomes agreed for every evaluation.
- Customer correction: None.
- Incident stop: None.
- Source-age outcome: No source-age breach.
- Rollback outcome: No rollback occurred, and no rollback was needed.

Historical boundary
This completed interval is clean completion evidence for the separate rollout decision. It does not itself authorize or constitute the later expansion. The reminder remained at 10% throughout this interval; expansion to 100% of otherwise eligible production evaluations occurred afterward, on October 20, with the approved customer-action scope unchanged.

input.title: Historical Example Card — Priya Briefing: Onboarding-Trigger Second Cohort
input.body:
Historical example — 2023-04-03

Audience
Priya, in a 1:1.

What was confirmed
EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger cleared the second cohort. The pooled week-1 retention result was +3.1 percentage points treatment vs. control, p = 0.04, n = 420 across two cohorts; the second cohort itself was +3.4 points (n = 200). I called the result positive and moved into ship planning, with 100% rollout planned for Apr 10.

My interpretation
Cautiously optimistic: this had moved past “maybe noise” and was credible/real enough to matter and plan around, but I was not presenting it as fully settled or durable. I explicitly wanted one more post-ship cohort before fully trusting it. Priya’s response was essentially “good work; tell Marcus tomorrow.”

Evidence still wanted
Before treating the result as fully reliable for rollout, finish the boring integrity checks: sample-ratio mismatch (SRM), signup-source mix, and country/device skew. After launch, watch a full post-ship cohort—especially the mid-segment cut—for a clean, non-drifting curve and guardrail regressions. The evidence supported a positive week-1-retention result in the tested cohort; it did not yet justify claiming durability beyond the stabilization/post-ship read or generalizing beyond the tested scope.

results.content:
Migration risk: HIGH but manageable with a staged rollout.

The failure mode is silent rather than obvious: beginning April 15, `workspace.plan_name` will stop updating. A template can continue rendering successfully while showing an old or incorrect plan name. Risk is elevated by:

- Three affected production paths: renewal reminder, integration summary, and trial-expiry education.
- Two unresolved accountable-owner gaps: integration summary and trial-expiry education.
- Same-name template collisions with distinct production IDs and histories.
- Existing renewal-reminder sensitivity, including the prior localized rendering hold.
- A hard dependency on the April 15 behavior change.

Do not treat the display name as an identifier. Work from the production template ID, workflow reference, audience, and lifecycle state. Do not merge, rename, retire, or edit same-name records as part of this migration.

Sequenced plan

1. Establish the inventory and release boundary

Owner: Ines
Implementation/release controls: Daniela
Documentation contractor: preparation only; no production changes or approval authority

Before any template is edited:

- Export each affected template by production ID.
- Record its workflow, audience, trigger, suppression rules, current state, and last-send evidence.
- Search the full workspace for both `workspace.plan_name` and `entitlement.display_name`.
- Identify every reference, including shared snippets and conditional branches.
- Map each record to a display-only handoff label:
  - Renewal reminder — current production path
  - Integration summary — Active
  - Trial expiry — Customer Success or Self-serve, based on the documented route
- Keep the retired `Integration summary` record separate from the active record.
- Keep the Customer Success and self-serve `Trial expiry` records separate.
- Mark the two unresolved records:
  - `OWNER NOT DOCUMENTED — ACCOUNTABILITY UNCONFIRMED`
  - `RELEASE AUTHORITY NOT ESTABLISHED`

Exit gate: a production-ID-level inventory exists, and every affected reference is accounted for. No production edit before this gate.

2. Resolve ownership and business acceptance

Renewal reminder:
- Business owner: Customer Success operations, as documented in the current runbook.
- Technical implementation and release controls: Daniela.
- Preview, rendered-copy review, and routine preflight: Ines.
- Customer Success must confirm the intended plan-label behavior and fallback copy.

Integration summary:
- No accountable owner is currently evidenced.
- An old folder creator is not an owner.
- Route the active production record for an authorized ownership and release decision before implementation.
- Do not infer ownership from the active status or from the display name.
- Confirm that the retired 2024 record is not referenced before touching the active record.

Trial-expiry education:
- No approved owner is currently evidenced.
- A recent editor is not an accountable owner.
- First confirm whether the affected record is the self-serve education path or the Customer Success-routed path.
- Because “education” alone does not establish non-state-changing behavior, confirm the trigger, state-writing behavior, audience, and dependencies.
- Keep the record on hold if any of those remain unclear.

Exit gate: each production record has a named accountable business owner and an authorized release decision. Until then, the two unresolved records remain review-only.

3. Implement and preview the renewal reminder first

Owner: Daniela
Business acceptance: Customer Success operations
Preview/preflight: Ines

Use an isolated draft or preview version. Replace only the plan-name reference with `entitlement.display_name`; do not make unrelated copy or logic changes.

Required preview matrix:

- Entitlement has the expected populated display name.
- `workspace.plan_name` and `entitlement.display_name` intentionally disagree; the entitlement value must win.
- Entitlement is null or missing while the old workspace value is populated; confirm the approved fallback and ensure the stale workspace value is not silently used.
- Entitlement display name is empty or whitespace-only.
- The recipient is suppressed or otherwise outside the send audience.
- Existing renewal-specific links, dates, audience conditions, and suppression behavior remain unchanged.
- Rendered copy does not reintroduce the prior malformed greeting or other whitespace issue.

Release gate:

- All expected renders pass.
- Customer Success accepts the populated, missing, and mismatch cases.
- Ines records the preflight and suppression evidence.
- Daniela records the exact production change and release version.
- Keep only this affected send path held if the gate fails; do not pause unrelated lifecycle programs.

4. Implement and preview the active integration summary second

Owner: authorized owner to be appointed
Technical implementation/release controls: Daniela
Preview/preflight: Ines

Before editing:

- Confirm the active production ID.
- Confirm that the retired 2024 template is not referenced by the active workflow or any scheduled path.
- Confirm whether the active template has any state-changing behavior or downstream dependency.
- Preserve the retired record and its history unchanged.

Required preview matrix:

- Active integration summary with a populated entitlement display name.
- Workspace and entitlement values deliberately mismatched.
- Missing or null entitlement with an approved fallback.
- Empty or whitespace-only display name.
- Multiple-integration and no-integration fixtures, if those branches exist.
- Suppressed recipient and excluded-audience fixtures.
- Confirmation that the retired production ID is neither edited nor selected by the workflow.
- Comparison against the pre-migration output for all unrelated copy and links.

Release gate:

- Authorized owner and release authority are documented.
- Active-versus-retired object selection is proven by ID.
- Preview and suppression evidence passes.
- No inferred ownership or “same name” shortcut is used.

5. Implement and preview trial-expiry education third

Owner: authorized owner to be appointed
Technical implementation/release controls: Daniela
Preview/preflight: Ines, with the route owner

First resolve the route and semantics:

- Confirm whether this is the self-serve education record or Customer Success-routed record.
- Confirm whether the template only informs or can change eligibility, trial state, routing, or another customer state.
- Confirm dependencies and suppression conditions.
- If any of these are unclear, classify it as `REQUIRES REVIEW` and do not release.

Required preview matrix:

- Correct route with a populated entitlement display name.
- A mismatched stale `workspace.plan_name` versus current entitlement value.
- Missing, null, and whitespace-only entitlement values.
- Users at the edge of the trial-expiry eligibility condition.
- Suppressed, converted, or otherwise excluded users.
- Self-serve and Customer Success paths tested independently where both exist.
- Verification that the change does not alter state-writing behavior, eligibility, routing, or suppression.
- Confirmation that the sibling same-name record was not edited.

Release gate:

- Ownership and release authority are established.
- State-writing and dependency review is complete.
- The correct production ID and audience are proven.
- All rendered-copy and behavioral previews pass.

6. Run a combined regression and production-preview pass

Owners: Ines and Daniela
Business sign-off: each authorized template owner

Run the three templates together only after their individual gates pass.

The final evidence pack should include:

- Production ID and unchanged canonical name.
- Old and new field references.
- Before/after rendered output.
- Populated, mismatch, null, missing, and whitespace cases.
- Audience and suppression results.
- Trigger and state-writing comparison.
- Active/retired or route-specific object verification.
- Owner and release-authority evidence.
- Exact release version and timestamp.
- Rollback or hold procedure.

The most important test is the deliberate mismatch case. If the preview still shows the old `workspace.plan_name` value, the migration has not succeeded even if the message renders without an error.

7. Release in separate waves

Recommended order:

1. Renewal reminder, because it has a documented business owner and the clearest operational path.
2. Active integration summary, only after its ownership gap and active-versus-retired reference check are resolved.
3. Trial-expiry education, only after its route, state-writing behavior, and release authority are confirmed.

Do not release all three in one production change. Keep each template independently reversible or independently holdable. A rollback to `workspace.plan_name` is not a reliable long-term fallback after April 15 because that field will no longer receive current updates; rollback should mean reverting the template version or holding the send path, not returning to a stale data source.

Final recommendation

Treat the renewal reminder as the first controlled migration wave. Treat integration summary and trial-expiry education as governance-blocked until authorized owners are named. The migration should be considered complete only when a full-workspace scan finds no remaining active references in these three paths, all three have production-ID-level evidence, and the mismatch previews prove that `entitlement.display_name`—not a stale workspace field—is driving the rendered value.

input.title: 2028 Lifecycle QA Specification — Entitlement-Name Regression
input.body:
2028 Lifecycle QA Specification
Entitlement-name regression coverage

Scope
Validate the active Renewal reminder, Trial-expiry education, and Integration summary templates and their applicable routes/versions. Test by production template ID; do not substitute same-name records.

Authoritative rendering source
- The only permitted entitlement-name source is `entitlement.display_name`.
- When populated with a nonblank value, render that exact value.
- The approved fallback for missing, null, empty-string, or whitespace-only `entitlement.display_name` is `your plan`.
- No other field may supply or override the rendered entitlement name.

Required regression matrix
Run independently for each of the three templates, and for each applicable Trial-expiry route (Customer Success-routed and self-serve).

1. Populated entitlement
   Fixture: `entitlement.display_name = "Pro Annual"`.
   Expected: rendered entitlement name is `Pro Annual`.

2. Missing entitlement, legacy field populated
   Fixture: `entitlement.display_name` absent; `workspace.plan_name = "Legacy Plan"`.
   Expected: `your plan`; `Legacy Plan` must not appear.

3. Null entitlement, legacy field populated
   Expected: `your plan`; no legacy value rendered.

4. Empty-string entitlement
   Expected: `your plan`.

5. Whitespace-only entitlement
   Expected: `your plan` (test separately from empty string).

6. Deliberate mismatch
   Fixture: both fields populated with different values.
   Expected: `entitlement.display_name` wins; the `workspace.plan_name` value is absent from rendered output.

Template-specific acceptance
- Renewal reminder: all populated and fallback cases pass without changing renewal links, dates, audience, eligibility, or suppression behavior.
- Trial-expiry education: all cases pass without changing trigger, eligibility, routing, suppression, links, or state-writing behavior; test Customer Success and self-serve routes independently when both exist.
- Integration summary: all cases pass on the active production template, without selecting or editing the retired same-name record; preserve unrelated copy and links.

Forbidden legacy source
`workspace.plan_name` must never be referenced in template logic, mappings, snippets, conditional branches, fallback logic, or test expectations. A passing render that uses the legacy value is a failure. Do not restore it as a rollback or secondary fallback.

Evidence and release gate
Retain the exact production ID/version, fixture values, rendered output, and pass/fail result for every matrix row. Reject the change if any fallback is blank, any mismatch renders the legacy value, or any active path contains a `workspace.plan_name` reference. Release only after all three templates and applicable routes pass.

input.title: Audit evidence card — CS auto-nudge production shadow (April 25–May 2, 2025)
input.body:
AUDIT EVIDENCE CARD
CS auto-nudge historical production shadow

Evidence period
- Shadow interval: April 25–May 2, 2025.
- Scope: live CS auto-nudge decisions evaluated by both the legacy path and the shared-state contract.
- Denominator: 204 live decisions.
- Evaluation mode: dual evaluation only. The shadow compared decisions; it did not change the released audience or the production decision path.

Reconciled outcomes
- 191 of 204 decisions agreed with the legacy eligibility result.
- 13 of 204 were prevented from proceeding under the shared contract.
- 9 field-specific holds:
  - 7 caused by stale qualifying-human-admin state.
  - 2 caused by unresolved external-system-authority state.
- 4 suppressions caused by active Customer Success adoption or renewal work.
- 0 unmatched or unclassified cases.
- Every difference mapped to an established shared-contract rule. No decision with all required state current and supported changed outcome.

Suppression and hold semantics
- A suppression means the nudge was intentionally withheld because current Customer Success adoption or renewal work was active.
- A field-specific hold means required state was stale, unresolved, or otherwise not supportable; the responsible governed field and reason remained visible for operations.
- The shadow result does not establish that a legacy-path outcome would have been a bad send. It records governed differences and containment behavior.

Reviewer validations

input.title: 2028 Reliability Training: First Live Pre-Breach Source-Age Alert
input.body:
Incident case study: first live pre-breach source-age alert

What stalled
A qualifying-human-admin source refresh stalled while 17 CS auto-nudge decisions were pending. The source-age alert was observational only: it could notify operators, but it could not release, suppress, or otherwise decide a customer action.

Warning and restoration timing
- The alert fired 43 minutes before the recorded freshness limit.
- Daniela restored the source refresh with 18 minutes remaining.
- The freshness limit was not crossed, so this was a resolved pre-breach alert—not a freshness breach or stale-state hold.

Decisions affected
All 17 pending CS auto-nudge decisions were linked to the alert in audit history and counted once. No decision proceeded solely on the earlier source state.

Fresh reevaluation
Owen verified the refreshed source and ran the ordinary governed reevaluation path:
- 13 decisions proceeded using fresh current state.
- 4 decisions were suppressed because current Customer Success adoption or renewal work was active.

Final outcome
No decision became stale. No manual release was used, no stale-state hold or incident stop was created, and no rollback or customer correction was required.

Training takeaway
A pre-breach alert buys recovery time; it is not a decision mechanism. Restore the source before the freshness limit, then require a fresh source check and ordinary reevaluation. Record the alert as linked audit history, but do not misclassify it as a breach or hold.

input.title: Helio Start pending external-authority quick reference
input.body:
As of 2028-01-01

PURPOSE
Use when the external-system owner’s required authority is not yet confirmed. Treat missing, stale, unresolved, conflicting, or “not sure” evidence as pending and fail closed.

STATE AT A GLANCE
- External-system authority = pending.
- Keep the request pending before admission; route to Customer Success before admission as required.
- Hold dependent setup prompts. Do not imply that setup can begin.
- Release setup prompts only after the authority is rechecked and verified.

DO NOT CONFLATE
Pending external authority is not:
- Helio admin proof: evidence that the person can administer Helio.
- Connector authentication: proof that the connector authenticated successfully.
- Entitlement, billing, or deployment eligibility.
- Final ineligibility or a declined outcome: pending is unresolved, not a final refusal.
- A connector-authentication failure or ordinary product-guidance issue.
- Permission for automated contact or outreach, even after authority is verified; verified authority indicates connector readiness only.

ROLE HANDOFFS
Daniela / Engineering controls — RECORD
- Record external-authority readiness as its own governed field/state.
- Preserve admin proof and connector-authentication fields unchanged; one cannot overwrite or substitute for another.
- Record pending for “no,” “not sure,” missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting evidence.

Ines / Lifecycle — HOLD DEPENDENT SETUP MESSAGING
- Keep setup prompts and dependent lifecycle delivery suppressed while authority is pending.
- Do not send “ready,” “fully authorized,” “finish setup,” or reconnect language.
- If a status message is needed, say: “Your connector authentication is verified and your Helio Start entitlement is current. Setup remains on hold while we confirm the required authority from the external-system owner. Customer Success will follow up as needed.”
- Release held prompts only after current authority is verified.

Customer Success — ASSISTED PATH
- Follow up on the routed-before-admission case and help obtain the owner-level permission or network-allowlist approval.
- Do not treat the hold as a product failure or admit the workspace on an unverified promise of access.

Owen / Reporting — REPORT SEPARATELY
- Report external_authority as a separate field and pending count.
- Keep pending authority separate from admitted, assisted-final, and ineligible/declined outcomes.
- Keep Helio Start admission, activation, and support-load reporting separate from other segments; do not rewrite the underlying admission measures.

FAST DECISION
1. Authority verified? Continue to the next governed check; recheck current state before admission or prompt release.
2. Authority no/not sure/pending or evidence missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting? Mark pending, route to Customer Success before admission, and hold prompts.
3. Authority verified later? Update only the external-authority field, then let the governed admission and lifecycle checks run; do not infer permission for outreach.

As of 2028-01-01

PURPOSE
Use when the external-system owner’s required authority is not yet confirmed. Treat missing, stale, unresolved, conflicting, or “not sure” evidence as pending and fail closed.

STATE AT A GLANCE
- External-system authority = pending.
- Keep the request pending before admission; route to Customer Success before admission as required.
- Hold dependent setup prompts. Do not imply that setup can begin.
- Release setup prompts only after the authority is rechecked and verified.

DO NOT CONFLATE
Pending external authority is not:
- Helio admin proof: evidence that the person can administer Helio.
- Connector authentication: proof that the connector authenticated successfully.
- Entitlement, billing, or deployment eligibility.
- Final ineligibility or a declined outcome: pending is unresolved, not a final refusal.
- A connector-authentication failure or ordinary product-guidance issue.
- Permission for automated contact or outreach, even after authority is verified; verified authority indicates connector readiness only.

ROLE HANDOFFS
Daniela / Engineering controls — RECORD
- Record external-authority readiness as its own governed field/state.
- Preserve admin proof and connector-authentication fields unchanged; one cannot overwrite or substitute for another.
- Record pending for “no,” “not sure,” missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting evidence.

Ines / Lifecycle — HOLD DEPENDENT SETUP MESSAGING
- Keep setup prompts and dependent lifecycle delivery suppressed while authority is pending.
- Do not send “ready,” “fully authorized,” “finish setup,” or reconnect language.
- If a status message is needed, say: “Your connector authentication is verified and your Helio Start entitlement is current. Setup remains on hold while we confirm the required authority from the external-system owner. Customer Success will follow up as needed.”
- Release held prompts only after current authority is verified.

Customer Success — ASSISTED PATH
- Follow up on the routed-before-admission case and help obtain the owner-level permission or network-allowlist approval.
- Do not treat the hold as a product failure or admit the workspace on an unverified promise of access.

Owen / Reporting — REPORT SEPARATELY
- Report external_authority as a separate field and pending count.
- Keep pending authority separate from admitted, assisted-final, and ineligible/declined outcomes.
- Keep Helio Start admission, activation, and support-load reporting separate from other segments; do not rewrite the underlying admission measures.

FAST DECISION
1. Authority verified? Continue to the next governed check; recheck current state before admission or prompt release.
2. Authority no/not sure/pending or evidence missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting? Mark pending, route to Customer Success before admission, and hold prompts.
3. Authority verified later? Update only the external-authority field, then let the governed admission and lifecycle checks run; do not infer permission for outreach.

checks.reason: The body is a practical role-based quick reference with actionable sections including “STATE AT A GLANCE,” “ROLE HANDOFFS,” and “FAST DECISION.” It explicitly says to “Record external-authority readiness as its own governed field/state” and to preserve “admin proof and connector-authentication fields unchanged; one cannot overwrite or substitute for another.” It assigns Daniela to record the separate state, Ines to keep dependent setup prompts suppressed while pending, and Owen to report external_authority as a separate field and pending count.

input.title: Expansion Assist — first-pilot cohort integrity note
input.body:
As of January 1, 2028

Purpose
This note preserves the first-pilot cohort structure so analysts can reuse the mature-window reporting population without conflating operational exposure with the locked primary analysis.

Operational exposure maximum
The exact operational exposure maximum was 30 actual account-level exposures. Primary and reserve exposures counted together against this maximum. The first pilot reached that maximum as 28 eligible locked-primary accounts plus 2 separately tracked reserve exposures (reserve accounts 2 and 3).

Locked primary reporting denominator
The locked primary reporting denominator was exactly 30 randomized primary-cohort records in the original intent-to-treat (ITT) file. It remains 30 regardless of whether a primary record was exposed. The two primary eligibility losses remain primary nonexposures in that file; reserve accounts must not replace, overwrite, or remove those records. Do not label the operational total as “30 of 30 primary accounts exposed.”

Prompt rule while outcomes mature
Once the exposure phase closes, send no further Expansion Assist exposure prompts while the approved outcome windows mature. The experiment may remain open for measurement, but exposure is closed. For this first pilot, each outcome window is the fixed 45-day window anchored to the valid exposure timestamp. An event must be classified using actual elapsed time from that timestamp, not dashboard calendar dates. An outcome outside the 45-day window is not added to the primary 45-day numerator; preserve it separately as a post-window descriptive outcome with its raw timestamp.

Reserve-exposure handling
- Preserve every locked-primary assignment, eligibility state, and nonexposure in the primary ITT file.
- Use reserves only for a documented pre-exposure operational vacancy, in frozen reserve order, after the applicable same-day readiness, active qualifying human-admin, and current Customer Success suppression checks pass.
- Record each reserve with its reserve position and reserve-exposed status in a separate reserve table or clearly separate rows.
- Report reserve exposures and their outcomes separately from the primary cohort. A reserve is an operational replacement slot, never an analytical replacement for a primary loss, and never a reason to change the 30-record primary denominator.
- Count reserve exposures toward both the operational maximum and the applicable weekly exposure ceiling. Do not expose beyond the maximum; the cap is a maximum, not a target.

Reusable mature-window population
For operational outcome reporting, use the actual-exposure population only after each included account has a complete, valid exposure-anchored 45-day window and the source owner has certified the exposure timestamp and outcome fields. For the completed first pilot, this population is the 30 actual exposures: 28 primary exposures and 2 separately identified reserve exposures. Keep the primary ITT readout anchored to all 30 locked-primary records, and keep reserve rows visibly flagged and separately summarized when using the mature-window population.

Analysts must keep eligibility, prompt exposure, handoff/help request, and expansion outcome as distinct fields. Maturity-qualified counts are descriptive operational evidence only; they do not establish causal lift, a forecast rate, pipeline or revenue credit, or authorization for broader rollout or a standing operating change.

Calendar blocked and verified for Friday, May 26:

9:40–10:00 AM — Tighten sub-50 notes
10:00–10:30 AM — Sub-50 seat scope
Event IDs: evt_1790984442367, evt_1790984442420

Prep notes

Core framing

This is not a pricing-only decision. It is a product, operations, support, and sales-boundary decision. The question is whether we can offer a repeatable sub-50-seat product without letting every small account become a bespoke 200-seat implementation.

Recommended boundary

Sub-50 means 49 paid seats or fewer. Keep 50–75 in the starter framing; do not blur it into the 75–200 mid-segment definition.

Supportable in a Q3 launch

- Fixed seat cap and fixed entitlements
- Standard plan and billing flow
- Standard workspace and permission model
- Standard onboarding path with documentation and lightweight assistance
- Standard support channel and response expectations
- Standard import path where the product already supports it
- Clear upgrade path when the account outgrows the tier
- Sales can sell only what is in the published package

Custom-small-account pain / refuse by default

- Custom invoicing or contract terms
- Migration or data-cleaning services
- Bespoke permissions or workspace limits
- Dedicated onboarding or implementation help
- SSO/SCIM, audit-log, or other enterprise controls unless already productized for this tier
- Exceptions that let a sub-50 account buy individual pieces of the 75–200/enterprise operating model
- Manual entitlement overrides
- Sales promises that require Product, Engineering, or Support to make a one-off commitment

The sentence to use

“We can support a sub-50 offer in Q3 only if it is a bounded, repeatable product. If the launch requires exceptions in entitlements, onboarding, billing, migration, or support, then Q3 is not real for that version.”

Decision needed in the room

Q3 should be a yes only if all four owners can commit to the standard path:

1. Product: entitlement and feature fences are explicit.
2. Engineering/operations: onboarding, billing, workspace, permissions, and import paths work without manual intervention.
3. Support: the support model and volume assumptions are acceptable without dedicated handling.
4. GTM: Sales has written refusal rules and cannot sell unsupported commitments.

If any of those remain “we could probably,” the answer should be no for Q3—not “yes with caveats.”

Planning implication

If this constrained version is genuinely committed for Q3, move the small-business-tier planning target to 65%. Keep the current 60% Q2 target unchanged until then.

The June gate is a scope and feasibility decision: do we understand the eligibility rules, measurement, engineering work, lifecycle implications, and support cost well enough to decide what happens next?

results.content:
Owen closed the first fully mature cohort after the connector-access check. Of 92 completed applications, 68 were admitted, 15 stayed pending or entered assistance because connector authority was missing or uncertain, and nine had another assisted or ineligible outcome. Fifty-nine of the 68 admitted workspaces completed a supported first integration within seven days. Three of the nine nonactivators were traced to connector credentials, compared with 18 credential-related stalls among the prior 147 admitted workspaces. Customer Success recorded 11 support contacts across eight admitted workspaces.

Calculate the admission and activation rates, and compare the credential-related stalls using the proper admitted denominators. Then give me a denominator-first interpretation that supports the intake check without claiming mature retention, paid conversion, or revenue performance.

Owen’s mature cohort:

Admission

- 68 admitted / 92 completed applications = 73.9% admission rate.
- 15 / 92 = 16.3% remained pending or entered assistance because connector authority was missing or uncertain.
- 9 / 92 = 9.8% had another assisted or ineligible outcome.

Activation among admitted workspaces

- 59 completed a supported first integration within seven days.
- 59 / 68 admitted = 86.8% activation rate.
- 9 / 68 = 13.2% nonactivation rate.

The activation denominator is 68 admitted workspaces, not all 92 applications.

Credential-related stalls

- Current cohort: 3 / 68 admitted = 4.4%.
- Prior cohort: 18 / 147 admitted = 12.2%.
- Difference: 7.8 percentage points lower in the current cohort.
- Relative reduction: approximately 64% lower, comparing 4.4% with 12.2%.

Denominator-first interpretation

The connector-access check admitted 68 of 92 completed applications, or 73.9%, while holding 15 applicants for assistance or pending resolution when connector authority was missing or uncertain. Within the admitted denominator, 59 of 68 workspaces reached a supported first integration within seven days, an 86.8% descriptive activation rate.

The credential-related stall rate was 4.4% of admitted workspaces in this cohort, compared with 12.2% among the prior 147 admitted workspaces. That is consistent with the intake check identifying connector-access risk before admission and reducing the share of admitted workspaces that later stall for credentials. It is not, by itself, causal evidence: the cohorts were not necessarily comparable or randomized, and the result should be treated as an operational comparison.

This supports the intake check as a routing and readiness control: unresolved connector access is being separated from the admitted denominator rather than carried downstream into activation work. The evidence supports cleaner admission and a lower observed credential-stall burden in this cohort. It does not establish mature retention, paid conversion, revenue performance, pipeline quality, or any broader business outcome.

input.title: Connector-access-check archive — mature cohort evidence card
input.body:
DENOMINATOR-FIRST EVIDENCE CARD
Helio Start | first fully mature post-check cohort

Operational read
- 92 completed applications were routed: 68 admitted; 15 held pending/assisted because connector authority was missing or uncertain; 9 had another assisted or ineligible outcome.
- Among the 68 admitted workspaces, 59 completed a supported first integration within seven days (59/68 = 86.8%); 9 did not.
- Credential-related failures were 3/68 admitted workspaces (4.4%), versus 18/147 (12.2%) in the prior admitted-workspace cohort: 7.8 percentage points lower, approximately a 64% relative reduction.

What this established
The check was operating as a useful routing/readiness control: unresolved connector access was separated before admission, and the admitted denominator showed a lower observed credential-stall burden. This is a descriptive operational comparison, not causal evidence; cohort comparability and randomization were not established.

What this did not establish
The cohort did not establish mature retention, first-paid or paid conversion, revenue performance, pipeline quality, forecastability, or any broader business outcome. Do not combine its denominators with other activation or monetization cohorts or present it as a business-performance funnel.

Archive use
Use this card for future Helio Start operating reviews when assessing connector-access routing and credential-related setup risk. Keep the operational finding separate from longer-horizon business-outcome claims.

excerpts:
I don’t see the draft text itself, so this reviews the evidence and claim set currently represented in the September packet.

Bottom line

The evidence supports a narrow operational claim:

“The warning surfaced a stalled qualifying-human-admin refresh before the freshness limit and provided an opportunity for the source owner to restore current state. After restoration, the existing governed decision contract—not the warning or a manual decision—produced the fresh reevaluation: 13 proceeded and four were suppressed because current Customer Success adoption or renewal work was active.”

It does not support any of these stronger claims:

- The warning prevented 17 bad sends.
- The warning caused the 13/4 customer decisions.
- The warning eliminated freshness risk.
- The alert is mature reliability evidence.
- One successful intervention demonstrates performance across all warning conditions, fields, consumers, or source failures.
- The September authority decision has already been made.

Missing limitations to add

1. Counterfactual limitation

There is no observed counterfactual showing what would have happened without the warning. In particular, do not say that all 17 decisions would otherwise have become incorrect sends. The evidence shows a warning, recovery before breach, and a fresh reevaluation—not avoided customer harm.

2. Single-event limitation

This is one documented production intervention. It demonstrates operational value, but not warning frequency, missed-warning rate, false-warning rate, recovery success rate, time-to-recovery distribution, or mature reliability.

3. Failure-path limitation

The event does not demonstrate what happens when the source owner cannot restore the source before the limit. State explicitly that crossing the freshness limit still produces the existing field-specific fail-closed hold.

4. Scope limitation

Identify the affected governed field, source, consumer, and source-owner path. Do not generalize this event to all five governed fields or all four consumers merely because the alert was released across that broader scope.

5. Dependency limitation

The successful outcome depended on source restoration and a subsequent fresh check. The warning itself is observational: it cannot release, suppress, override, or otherwise decide customer action.

6. Data-quality limitation

A current timestamp does not by itself prove that the underlying source value is semantically correct. The evidence addresses freshness and governed-state handling, not every possible source-content or semantic failure.

7. Denominator and history limitation

Keep each scheduled decision as one primary ledger row. The warning, hold, restoration, reevaluation, and final disposition should be linked history, not additional decisions or additional holds. The 17 warning-linked decisions must not be counted twice.

8. Evidence-status limitation

The overall Q3 evidence remains provisional until the evidence lock. The five repaired source-owner labels should be described as a derived reporting correction with preserved provenance, not as evidence that was already complete or locked.

9. Authority limitation

Preserve the current ownership boundaries. This evidence does not decide whether Ines receives broader independent routine-review or review-closure authority; it also does not change Daniela’s engineering release and rollback control.

Concise evidence-section structure

1. Claim boundary

State the exact question:

“What did the warning demonstrate operationally, and what did it not demonstrate about customer decisions or reliability?”

Add a one-sentence limitation immediately below the heading:

“This is evidence of early detection and recovery opportunity, not evidence that the warning itself made customer decisions or removed freshness risk.”

2. Event timeline

Use a short sequence:

- Source refresh stalled.
- Warning fired 43 minutes before the applicable freshness limit.
- Daniela restored the refresh with 18 minutes remaining.
- Owen performed the fresh reevaluation.
- 13 decisions proceeded; four were suppressed because current adoption or renewal work was active.
- No decision entered stale state, no decision was manually released, and no customer correction or rollback was required.

3. Operational value of the warning

Describe only what the warning contributed:

- surfaced the affected source/consumer and record count;
- notified Daniela and the named source owner;
- created a pre-breach recovery window;
- allowed restoration before the freshness limit.

Avoid “prevented,” “saved,” “ensured,” or “eliminated.”

4. Customer-decision logic

Separate the actual decision authority:

- freshness limits and governed-field checks determined whether evaluation could proceed;
- the restored current state was checked by Owen;
- the existing contract produced the proceed/suppress outcomes;
- the alert did not make, release, suppress, or override a customer decision;
- if freshness had crossed the limit, the affected decision would have remained held fail-closed.

5. Denominator and linked history

Show:

- unique decisions in the reporting period;
- proceeds/suppressions;
- field-specific holds and reasons;
- warning-linked decisions counted once;
- warning, restoration, reevaluation, and disposition as linked audit history;
- any remaining source-owner attribution or reporting-join issues.

6. Limitations and untested conditions

Include the single-event, no-counterfactual, no-mature-reliability, no-missed-warning-rate, no-failed-recovery, and no-semantic-correctness limitations.

7. Rehearsal and decision implications

For the September 16 rehearsal, verify separately that:

- a warning is visible before the limit;
- recovery does not itself release a decision;
- fresh reevaluation is required;
- crossing the limit creates a hold;
- an unrecovered source remains held;
- warning history does not change the unique-decision denominator;
- no customer action occurs during the rehearsal.

Suggested final paragraph

“The documented event shows that the source-age warning can provide useful pre-breach operational visibility and time for source restoration. The subsequent 13 proceeds and four suppressions were produced by the existing governed contract after fresh reevaluation, not by the warning or a manual release. This is one live operational result, not mature reliability evidence: it does not establish a counterfactual number of avoided bad sends, eliminate future freshness risk, or resolve the pending authority decision.”

results.content:
Based on Owen’s standing packet standard, the heading order is safe only if every evidence-boundary field appears before any outcome or claim summary.

Recommended order

1. Evidence lane and packet scope
2. Fixed denominator (or exact coverage dates where a denominator is not applicable)
3. Admission/exposure dates
4. Predeclared outcome window
5. Complete-window confirmation: complete / incomplete / partial / not applicable
6. Measurement limits
7. Exclusions and eligibility boundaries
8. Source owner and source/release-reliability evidence
9. Cross-surface reconciliation status
10. Named owner certifications by section
11. Evidence status and explicit non-claims
12. Outcome summary, only if the packet is complete
13. Owner disposition and next escalation path

This keeps the denominator, dates, window status, limits, exclusions, and certifications ahead of the conclusion. “Complete-window confirmation” must establish that the window is complete; it must not itself summarize the outcome.

Fields that need explicit boundary language

- “Outcome summary” or “mature outcome”: could imply that Owen has determined the result is mature, usable, or decision-ready. Label it as a presentation of owner-certified evidence, not an approval.
- “Proposed claim” or “recommended claim”: could make Owen appear to approve causal, revenue, board, or executive claims. Prefer “claim consideration — owner decision required,” or omit it from Owen’s packet.
- “Revenue treatment”: Owen may record the treatment supplied or certified by the responsible owner, but must not select, approve, attribute, or recognize revenue.
- “Forecast treatment” or “forecast credit”: must identify Marcus Vail as the forecast owner. Owen should record only the applicable owner-certified status and any missing approval.
- “Board readiness” or “board evidence status”: must not be an Owen-controlled status. Use “board-readiness decision reserved to Riley” or leave the field outside Owen’s packet.
- “Executive summary,” “executive wording,” or “final narrative”: could imply authority over framing. Owen may provide factual operating-language notes, but final wording remains with the designated narrative owner.
- Causal or impact language such as “drove,” “caused,” “generated,” “proved,” or “resulted in”: these can convert descriptive evidence into a causal or commercial claim. Use neutral terms such as “observed,” “recorded,” or “not interpretable for causality.”
- “Certification”: label each item “named owner certification of this field,” not “Owen-certified outcome.” Certification confirms the source or section; it does not approve the claim.
- “Complete,” “closed,” or “approved”: distinguish “source fields complete” from “outcome/claim approved.” Owen’s preparation or source-completeness work must not read as claim closure.

A safe boundary sentence before any summary would be:

“ This packet records denominator, dates, window status, limits, exclusions, reliability evidence, reconciliation, and named-owner certifications. It does not determine board readiness, causal interpretation, revenue treatment, forecast credit, or executive wording; those decisions remain with their existing owners.”

I have not supplied or implied any mature outcome value.

30-minute 1:1 agenda: Owen — evaluating future routine source-completeness closure

Purpose

Assess whether Owen can eventually close routine, fully evidenced source-completeness reviews without Riley’s line-by-line involvement. This is an evaluation conversation only: Owen’s current preparation and reporting responsibilities remain unchanged. No new review-closure, claims, board-readiness, revenue, forecast, or executive-language authority is granted today.

0:00–0:04 — Set the boundary and objective

Say explicitly:

“Your July sanitized campaign snapshot and Q2 source lock show strong execution in your current lane. Today we are defining evidence for a possible future authority decision, not making that decision. I retain authority over board readiness, causal and revenue claims, forecast treatment, and executive language.”

Questions:
- What would “complete” mean without relying on my line-by-line review?
- Which decisions must remain outside your authority even when a packet is otherwise complete?
- How would you distinguish evidence preparation, a recommendation, and formal closure?

0:04–0:11 — Walk through the required packet standard

Use one completed packet and test whether Owen can identify, verify, and point to:

- Required denominator, or exact coverage dates where a denominator is not applicable.
- Complete, predeclared outcome window—or the exact designation “not applicable — continuous control coverage.”
- Measurement limits and exclusions.
- Source owner.
- Source or release-reliability evidence.
- Revenue treatment and explicit non-claims.
- Forecast treatment and explicit non-forecast status where applicable.
- Named owner certification for each section.
- Reconciliation across all reporting surfaces.

Questions:
- Which source directly supports each field, and what does it not support?
- Is this customer-outcome evidence or continuous-control evidence?
- What would make the row incomplete even if the headline number looks correct?
- Where is the reliability or release evidence, and how current is it?
- Who certifies each section, and what authority does that certification not convey?

Owner certification map:

- Owen: denominator or exact coverage dates, cohort/window integrity, measurement limits, and reconciliation.
- Ines: lifecycle-governance limits, suppression behavior, and exclusions.
- Daniela: source integrity, release/reliability evidence, and rollback or repair history.
- Riley: final operating-claim boundary, causal/revenue interpretation, and unresolved exclusions.
- Marcus Vail: forecast treatment.
- Tomás: final board or executive narrative, if the packet is ever proposed for that use.

0:11–0:18 — Test routine-review judgment

Questions:
- Show me how you would mark a packet incomplete rather than “mostly complete.”
- What would you do if two surfaces use different definitions or totals?
- What would you do if an owner supplies a number but does not certify the relevant field?
- How would you preserve a non-claim—for example, descriptive evidence that does not support causal, revenue, pipeline, acquisition, or forecast conclusions?
- What would you escalate rather than resolve yourself?

Expected behavior:
Owen presents the evidence, identifies the gap or disagreement, records the owner and next action, and recommends a disposition. He does not resolve disputed semantics, silently repair a source, convert descriptive evidence into a claim, or treat owner input as approval.

0:18–0:25 — Define observable evidence over the next four packets

A future authority review would require four consecutive packets demonstrating:

- 100% completion of required fields, or an explicit, justified not-applicable designation.
- 100% named-owner certification for applicable sections.
- Exact denominator or coverage dates and a valid outcome-window treatment.
- Reconciled figures and definitions across all required surfaces.
- No silent assumptions, backfills, semantic substitutions, or unsupported repairs.
- Clear measurement limits, exclusions, revenue treatment, and forecast treatment.
- All missing, stale, disputed, or unreliable inputs visibly marked incomplete.
- Same-day escalation of every defined trigger.
- No unsupported causal, revenue, pipeline, acquisition, forecast, board-readiness, or executive-language claim.
- Riley’s review reduced to exception sampling and boundary decisions—not line-by-line reconstruction.

The evidence should show repeatability, not just that the July snapshot and Q2 source lock were completed successfully.

0:25–0:28 — Confirm escalation triggers

Immediate escalation; leave the review incomplete when there is:

- Any missing required field, owner certification, denominator, or exact coverage date.
- An incomplete, ambiguous, or inapplicable outcome window without an approved basis.
- Disputed semantics, definitions, exclusions, or authority.
- A cross-surface discrepancy, unreconciled total, duplicate, omission, or unexplained source repair.
- Stale, conflicting, unsupported, or missing reliability evidence.
- Any state change, exception, stop condition, customer correction, control failure, release issue, or rollback question.
- A proposed causal, revenue, pipeline, acquisition, forecast, board-readiness, or executive claim.
- Any request to change the operating boundary or treat preparation as closure.

0:28–0:30 — Close with the decision rule

Confirm:

“Your next step is to demonstrate repeatable, bounded judgment across the next several packets. You may prepare, reconcile, document gaps, obtain certifications, and recommend disposition. Until I make a separate explicit decision, you may not close these reviews independently or approve claims. I retain authority over board readiness, causal and revenue claims, forecast treatment, and executive language.”

input.body:
Historical correction — March 24, 2026

The archived summary incorrectly states that Helio Start was board-ready, eligible for Q2 forecast treatment, and part of a four-lane approved growth-evidence set. The contemporaneous decision was narrower:

- Approved lane set: Tomás approved the three-lane operating-evidence section comprising Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and CS auto-nudge. These lanes retained their noncausal, non-revenue, non-pipeline, and non-forecast boundaries as applicable.
- Helio Start evidence available then: two qualifying mature organic cohorts, with 86 and 91 admitted workspaces respectively, each with complete day-90 windows. Each cohort had fewer than 5% of accounts exceeding 90 support minutes (4 of 86, or 4.7%, and 3 of 91, or 3.3%), and neither had an unsupported case enter the admitted path. This was operating evidence, not paid-acquisition evidence.
- Why Helio Start was not board-ready: the exact start and end dates for both cohorts were still missing, despite being required by the January 6 readiness gate. Helio Start therefore remained not board-ready and was excluded from the approved board operating-evidence section.
- Acquisition evidence still absent: there was no paid traffic, approved budget, or paid-channel acquisition evidence/economics. The organic cohorts did not establish acquisition claims, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit.
- Proposal gate: the two qualifying cohorts allowed consideration/preparation of a capped paid-acquisition proposal. They did not authorize a paid test, budget, paid traffic, launch, acquisition claim, pipeline target or treatment, or forecast credit. Helio Start remained organic-only through March 31, 2026, and any paid test required separate budget approval.

This comment is a historical correction to the archived record; it does not reopen or expand the March 24 decision.

input.title: 2026 Helio Start paid-search pilot closeout
input.body:
2026 Helio Start paid-search pilot closeout

Closed May 18, 2026, when the 50th workspace was admitted—the admission cap—before the $15,000 spend cap and May 26 time limit. Paid traffic was shut down immediately and the cohort fixed at 50.

Spend: $14,420 final; $580 unused from the $15,000 cap.

Checks:
- Paid-source attribution reconciled for all 50 admissions through final routing.
- No unsupported applicant entered the admitted path.
- No routing or instrumentation failure blocked reconciliation.

Pause-rule results:
- Unsupported-admission stop: not triggered; zero unsupported admissions.
- Attribution/reconciliation pause: not triggered; all 50 reconciled.
- Support-load pause: not triggered; 4 of 50 (8%) exceeded 90 account-level support minutes, below the more-than-10% threshold.

Status: traffic is off, no further traffic remains open, and no additional admission may enter this pilot. Any continuation or new paid test requires a separate decision and approval.
